title: SEMO to honor Freezes as 2026 Friends of the University
text:
EducationMarch 4, 2026
SEMO to honor Freezes as 2026 Friends of the University
SEMO will honor longtime supporters Dr. John and Martha Freeze as its 2026 Friends of the University, recognizing more than 40 years of giving, including a pre-dental scholarship.
Southeast Missouri State University announced Dr. John Freeze and Mrs. Martha Freeze will be recognized as its 2026 Friends of the University.
According to a SEMO news release, the Freezes will be honored with the Friends of the University award on Friday, March 27, at the President's Council Dinner. The release states that both Martha and John have supported the university for more than 40 years, which includes funding a pre-dental scholarship to support aspiring dentists. The release also notes that a recent scholarship recipient invited the Freezes to her graduation celebration, where they met two past recipients who are now practicing dentists.
"It showed how all those years of donating really added up," John Freeze states in the release.
The Freezes became early supporters of the Copper Dome in 1984 and continued to give consistently. John Freeze states in the release that earlier on, they gave the minimum for Copper Dome, but increased it as they were able to.
“At that time, it was still significant. As we were able, we increased it. The more people who give, the more it’s going to help. It builds up," John Freeze states in the release.
The Freezes have been longtime supporters of the university beyond donating. The release states John Freeze's father played football at SEMO and he attended games while growing up. John Freeze also attended the campus school before enrolling as a college student. John Freeze earned a Bachelor of Science in zoology from SEMO and then came back to Cape Girardeau in 1980 to build his dental practice after graduating from the University of Missouri-Kansas City School of Dentistry.
The release states Martha Freeze was from Jackson and grew up attending SEMO football games as well. Martha Freeze received a Bachelor of Science in education with an emphasis in physical education, and all four of her siblings earned degrees from the institution. According to the release, after 51 years of marriage, the Freezes have two daughters, including a SEMO graduate and two grandchildren, as well as extended family members who are SEMO alumni.
"We’ve been so blessed by what God’s provided for us, and we wanted to help others, so we decided to focus our giving on SEMO," Martha Freeze states in the release.
The release states John Freeze has served in several board member and leadership roles across his career, including serving on the Missouri Dental Association, the Southeast Dental Society, the Cape Dental Study Club, the Lutheran Home Board and GROWS Implant Study Club. John Freeze currently serves as chair of the Public Health Center, is a member of the Oral Health Coalition and also serves on the SEMO Foundation Board. John Freeze sold his practice in 2014 to a SEMO graduate before retiring in 2017.
